map.隧道瓦斯监测参考 使用指南: Tunnel Gas Monitoring Reference User Guide
map.输入瓦斯浓度，查询安全等级与处置措施（依据《煤矿安全规程》《铁路瓦斯隧道技术规范: Enter the gas concentration to look up the safety grade and response measures (based on the 'Coal Mine Safety Regulations' and the 'Technical Code for Railway Gas Tunnels')
map.五级浓度分级与处置：<0.5% 安全（正常作业、持续监测）、0.5%~0.8%: Five-level concentration grading and response: <0.5% safe (normal work, continuous monitoring), 0.5%-0.8% caution (increase ventilation and monitoring frequency), 0.8%-1.0% alert (stop part of the work, withdraw non-essential personnel), 1.0%-1.5% danger (stop work, cut power, withdraw personnel), >=1.5% extreme danger (evacuate immediately, seal the working face, report for handling).
map.断电阈值：浓度达到或超过 1.0% 即判需立即切断电源；页面按监测位置（工作面/: Power-cut threshold: reaching or exceeding 1.0% means power must be cut immediately; the page marks monitoring points by location (working face/return airflow, general roadway, near electrical equipment), and all three thresholds are 1.0%.
map.爆炸性判定：浓度落在 5%~16% 区间判为处于爆炸浓度范围（极度危险）；低于: Explosiveness judgement: a concentration in the 5%-16% range is judged to be within the explosive range (extremely dangerous); below 5% is under the lower explosive limit and will not explode; above 16% is over the upper explosive limit and will not explode for lack of oxygen. The page shows the current interval with a five-segment colour bar (safe green / caution blue / alert yellow / danger red / extreme danger dark red).
map.算例：八个浓度点的分级与处置判定: Worked example: grading and response judgement for eight concentration points
map.：0.30% → 安全、正常作业持续监测、不断电、低于爆炸下限；0.50% →: : 0.30% -> safe, normal work with continuous monitoring, no power cut, below the lower explosive limit; 0.50% -> caution, increase ventilation and monitoring frequency, no power cut; 0.65% -> caution, same as above; 0.90% -> alert, stop part of the work and withdraw non-essential personnel, no power cut (has not reached 1.0%); 1.20% -> danger, stop work, cut power, withdraw personnel, power cut required; 2.00% -> extreme danger, evacuate immediately, seal the working face and report, power cut required; 8.00% -> extreme danger and within the explosive concentration range (5%-16%); 20.00% -> extreme danger, but above the upper explosive limit so it will not explode for lack of oxygen.
map.为什么规定瓦斯浓度达到 1.0% 就要断电撤人？: Why do the rules require cutting power and withdrawing people when gas concentration reaches 1.0%?
map.1.0% 远低于 5% 的爆炸下限，留出的余量用于应对监测滞后、局部积聚与浓度快: 1.0% is far below the 5% lower explosive limit, and the margin covers monitoring lag, local accumulation and rapid rises in concentration. Gas distribution underground is extremely uneven, and the roof, corners and stopped-airflow zones easily form local high concentrations, so when a monitoring point reads 1.0% the local level may already be far higher. That is why the rules require stopping work, cutting power and withdrawing personnel at 1.0%, ventilating first and re-testing until it passes before resuming, rather than waiting until it approaches the lower explosive limit.
map.浓度超过 16% 反而「不爆炸」，是不是就不危险了？: If the concentration exceeds 16% it 'will not explode' instead, so is it no longer dangerous?
map.不是。高于爆炸上限只是意味着该处混合气体因缺氧而无法被点燃，但极其危险：一是人员: No. Being above the upper explosive limit only means the mixture at that spot cannot be ignited because of lack of oxygen, but it is extremely dangerous: first, anyone entering can suffocate from lack of oxygen; second, once the gas mixes with fresh air and is diluted back into the 5%-16% range it instantly becomes an explosive mixture. Therefore high-concentration gas accumulation zones must be sealed off and entry strictly forbidden, and handling is done by a professional rescue team following gas drainage procedures with slow release and continuous monitoring of return airflow concentration.
